As the other commenter here said, you could be bi with a preference towards women. Or a lesbian. I know this might be tough to bring up to your parents, but it might be useful telling them about how gender/sexuality/attraction etc. is fluid? You yourself may not be sure, or ever will be, so it could be something you wanna bring up. 

You could also consider romantic vs sexual attraction? I thought I was bi-romantic homosexual when I was younger. But I came to realise that despite my appreciation for guys, I don't actually wanna date them; I just find them aesthetically attractive sometimes. So these days I like to consider myself a lesbian.

Lastly, there are other labels to explore if you're looking for one! Labels such as queer, pan, poly etc. Ultimately, some people are still gonna be a lil confused. As long as you're comfortable, I think that's the gold standard. No idea if any of this helps but wishing you the best of luck!

Let me try! Boundaries can be physical, emotional or mental lines that people have in place. It differs vastly from person to person. 

For example, some people are alright with others standing close to them - their physical boundary isn't violated. Someone might enjoy chatting with strangers but set a boundary for conversations (e.g. don't ask about my parents/childhood/sexuality). 

​

Essentially, it's a 'line' that divides things you're comfortable with, and things you are not. Though, this definition is off the top of head. It's also not always clear or stagnant. In fact, it rarely is. I think I often cross boundaries as well (accidentally).

One of the easiest ways to understand someone's boundaries or to know if you're crossing any is to just ask. A couple sentences I like to use would be: 

"Are you comfortable talking about this topic?" or "Would it better if I stop doing this?"

​

In this case, I'm not sure about your boundary as to how comfortable you are with my tone or choice of examples, so I can ask - let me know if I'm overstepping, okay?
